correctness.rationale: Exactly 32 distinct ten-bit squares uu with u in {0,1}^5 must appear in a linear word. Choosing ordered occurrences yields an overlap-weighted Hamiltonian path of all required length-10 squares; conversely every such path constructs a superstring by maximal overlaps. The 8 rotation necklaces (two singleton, six length five) entail q>=7 cross-necklace transitions; cross cost at least 6, within cost at least 1, hence L>=41+5q, excluding q>=9 at L<=81. If q=7, one contiguous block for each necklace; direct internal permutation minima by endpoints (<=5! permutations) and a subset DP over eight blocks gives global minimum 82. At q=8, L<=81 requires equality in every cost: all within-orbit edges are directed one-step rotations and each crossing costs 6; exactly one primitive necklace splits into two directed arcs. All 6*5*4=120 splits were exhaustively decided by a nine-block subset reachability DP, none feasible. The given literal 82-bit witness was independently checked to include each distinct ten-bit square. Reimplemented both DPs independently from the supplied VERIFY.py, obtaining q7=82, 120 q8 splits with zero equality cases, witness length 82 and 32 required squares. This is a finite exhaustive proof conditional on faithfully enumerated partitions and transitions, not extrapolated finite sampling.
